theorem.name: BOUNDED_WIDTH_LOW_INCIDENCE_PIVOT_IS_RAW_CAP_SAFE
theorem.statement: Let F be canonical with state size s<=C and maximum clause width w>=2. For pivot x let p,q be its positive/negative clause-incidence counts and d=p+q. If p=0 or q=0, elimination is pure deletion. Otherwise B_x<=s-(w+1)d+(2w-1)pq<=s-(w+1)d+(2w-1)d^2/4. Thus d<=D_w(Delta) guarantees a capped exact pivot, where Delta=C-s and D_w(Delta)=2*((w+1)+sqrt((w+1)^2+(2w-1)*Delta))/(2w-1).
proof: Insert those inequalities into the audited generic whole-state raw bound.
Solve ((2w-1)/4)d^2-(w+1)d-Delta<=0 on d>=0; its positive root is D_w(Delta).

corollary.name: AVERAGE_DEGREE_FORCES_A_SAFE_PIVOT
corollary.statement: sum_x d_x=L, hence min_x d_x<=L/n. Therefore L/n<=D_w(Delta) forces at least one ordinary exact capped pivot.
corollary.contrapositive_pressure: If every live pivot truly overflows, then d_x>D_w(Delta) for every x and L>n*D_w(Delta).
